title: "Roadmap"
subtitle: "Ten phases, six milestones, exit criteria instead of dates"
---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
This page summarises [CONCEPT.md §7](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/CONCEPT.md),
which is authoritative. Where the two disagree, CONCEPT.md is right and this page is stale.
:::

Recueil is written by one person, incrementally. Each phase is a shippable `0.x` release with an
**exit criterion** rather than a date, because dates set by a solo maintainer are fiction and exit
criteria are testable. Effort is relative: S, M, L, XL.

Phases 1 to 3 are the critical path, because they are what retires the stack currently in daily use
— Zotero with three self-written plugins, Paperless-ngx, and a pile of R scripts holding them
together.

## Phases

| Phase | Theme | Effort | Milestone |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0** | Spec and scaffold | M | — |
| **1** | Core library + Zotero migration | L | **M1** Zotero replaced |
| **2** | Ingestion + storage backends | M | **M2** Paperless replaced |
| **3** | Enrichment, checks, dedup | L | **M3** Plugins retired |
| **4** | Reading, search, desktop shell | M | — |
| **5** | Graph, bibliometrics, R/Python | L | **M4** Bibliometrics in R |
| **6** | Curated networks | M–L | — |
| **7** | Systematic review | XL | **M5** First SR end-to-end |
| **8** | Mobile + own connector | M | — |
| **9** | Community and 1.0 | M, ongoing | **M6** 1.0 |

## Phase 0 — Spec and scaffold

**Where the project is now.** ADRs 0001–0012 written and 0013–0020 decided; data model v1 with ERD,
migrations and a fixture library; the OpenAPI skeleton, plugin manifest schema and hook catalogue;
the monorepo scaffold, CI, Docker build, this documentation site, licence, `CITATION.cff` and
contribution guidance.

**Exit:** `recueil serve` returns health on an empty library, and the specification has been checked
against the three existing Zotero plugins with a documented answer to "can each be expressed as a
plugin?".

## Phase 1 — Core library and Zotero migration → M1

Items, documents, attachments, collections, tags, notes and custom fields on content-hash local
storage over SQLite. REST v1 for all of it, the CLI, the Docker image, backup and restore. A library
view, item pane and basic PDF viewing in the web UI. The Zotero importer with its verification
report, BibTeX, CSL-JSON and RIS export with stable citation keys, and the `.bib` endpoint. The
connector endpoint, so the Zotero Connector works unchanged.

**Exit:** own library imported at 100% item count with an attachment-hash coverage report; daily
capture via the connector; Overleaf building from the exported `.bib`; thirty days without launching
Zotero.

## Phase 2 — Ingestion and storage backends → M2

**In the tree.** The ten-stage pipeline of CONCEPT.md §5.3; watched folder, WebDAV and IMAP sources;
the scanner path as a folder or mailbox source; the YAML rule engine with its dry-run report; the
confidence gate and the review queue, with screens for sources, review and rules in the web client;
the Office facet; the Paperless-ngx importer and its verification report; the WebDAV and S3 storage
backends behind one conformance suite; PWA upload.

**Exit:** scanner to searchable item with zero manual steps; mail to library; Paperless-ngx
decommissioned after a verified import.

**Where that stands.** The first two were rehearsed against the repository's fixture corpora and
pass: six scans dropped into a watched folder became six searchable items in under two seconds
with nothing typed, and all eight fixture messages went through an in-process IMAP server into documents,
notes and rule-filed items. The Paperless importer reaches every count the fixture corpus states.

**M2 is not claimed**, because the criterion is about a real scanner, a real mailbox and a real
Paperless-ngx instance being switched off — none of which a fixture can stand in for. Two known
limits carry forward: the OCRmyPDF adapter exists but has never been run against a real OCRmyPDF
here, and the decision to OCR is taken per document rather than per page, so a scanned page inside an
otherwise digital PDF is missed.

## Phase 3 — Enrichment, checks, dedup → M3

The resolver framework across every source, with field-level provenance, merge policy and metrics
time series. The checks engine, report export and bibliography audit mode. File and record dedup
with a rules UI and dry-run reports. Plugin SDK v1, with all of the above shipped as first-party
plugins, and the compatibility test suite.

**Exit:** parity tests against Metadata Mender, Attaclone-dedup and Argus One pass on the fixture
library; those plugins archived; one real manuscript review delivered with a reference audit report.

## Phase 4 — Reading, search, desktop shell

Annotations as records and the PDF.js annotation layer, with export to embedded PDF annotations.
FTS5 and Meilisearch; saved searches as smart collections. The GROBID sidecar, feeding Phase 5.
Tauri desktop v1 with watched folders, a tray, the URI scheme and open-in-external-app — including a
PDF.js performance test on WebKitGTK, which is the known risk on Linux.

**Exit:** annotate, note and cite works entirely inside the application, in the browser and in the
desktop shell.

## Phase 5 — Graph, bibliometrics, R and Python → M4

Edge providers, shadow works, the local citation network, derived networks and budgeted deep dives.
The vocabulary layer with MeSH tree import and thesaurus maps. The analytics Parquet export, DuckDB
attach, and in-app Sigma.js maps carrying coverage statistics. R package v0.1 and Python package
v0.1.

**Exit:** `rc_bibliometrix()` output runs in biblioshiny unmodified; a VOSviewer map renders from
the export; the local citation network of the library renders in-app.

## Phase 6 — Curated networks

The CuratedNetwork document model, the Cytoscape.js editor, annotations, versions and freezing.
Exports to SVG, PDF and PNG, GraphML, GEXF and JSON, TikZ, and tidygraph.

**Exit:** one publication figure produced end to end, in-app or via `ggraph`, per
[ADR-0013](adr.qmd).

## Phase 7 — Systematic review → M5

In order: sources, import and dedup with source tracking → title and abstract screening → the PRISMA
counter → full-text retrieval and screening → export to `meta`, `metafor`, PRISMA2020 and `robvis` →
extraction forms → risk-of-bias templates → snowballing via deep dive → the Quarto report template.
This phase gets its own specification before any work starts.

**Exit:** a real review run start to finish; the PRISMA flow exported from live counts; extraction
data loading in R without manual reshaping.

## Phase 8 — Mobile and own connector

Tauri mobile, with Capacitor as the fallback: camera scan, barcode lookup, share sheet, cached
reading and queued writes. Recueil's own WebExtension superseding the Zotero Connector, published to
the Chrome Web Store, AMO and Safari.

**Exit:** phone capture to library in under thirty seconds; the extension listed in the Chrome Web
Store.

## Phase 9 — Community and 1.0 → M6

The plugin registry and `create-recueil-plugin`; this documentation site complete; a demo library.
Release hygiene: citation blocks, `CITATION.cff`, a Zenodo DOI, multi-arch images, upgrade
guarantees, a security review. Governance: public roadmap, DCO, issue templates, and the groundwork
for multi-user.

**Exit:** the 1.0 tag; plugin API v1 frozen; at least one plugin not written by the maintainer.

## Sequencing rules

- Phase 6 and Phase 7 never start before Phase 5's graph schema is in production.
- Phases 4 and 5 may interleave. Phase 8 is cheap once the API is stable.
- **Any scope addition to a phase removes something else from it, or goes to the parking lot.** Scope
  is zero-sum; this is the rule that keeps a solo project shippable.

## Openness

The repository is public and AGPL from the first commit, but the project is developed as a tool for
its author through **M3** and opens properly at **M4** ([ADR-0014](adr.qmd)). Until then there is no
support commitment and no roadmap promise. Bug reports, reproductions and corrections to the
specification are welcome now; large unsolicited pull requests are likely to be declined.

## Parking lot

Post-1.0, in no order: Word, LibreOffice and Google Docs integration via Zotero's integration
protocol · multi-reviewer screening with conflict resolution · an embeddings-based similarity plugin
· a citation-intent UI · Wikidata and Wikicite sync · OpenAlex topic clustering · altmetrics · HTML
snapshot annotation · a Quarto extension · LLM-assisted screening with per-decision disclosure · an
Overleaf git bridge for `.bib` sync.

## The risks that would actually derail it

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Scope creep | Non-goals are written down; one spec per phase; additions are zero-sum |
| Dependency on Zotero translators and translation-server | Pinned versions; identifier-based fallback import via Crossref and OpenAlex; own connector in Phase 8 |
| API policy changes at OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar | Resolver abstraction, caching, key support, more than one source per fact |
| Citation coverage gaps producing misleading maps | Provenance and coverage statistics beside every map |
| Solo sustainability | Small releases, boring technology, documentation from day one, every phase independently useful |
| Data loss in migration | Idempotent importers, verification reports, Zotero read-only until M1 is confirmed |
